market.question: Will the 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.10% in September?

en.title: Yield Hits 5.10%, Probability Soars
en.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield has explicitly hit 5.10% in September, driving the market probability to 100%. This surge was fueled by strong inflation fears from rising input costs and hawkish Fed sentiment.
drivers: 10-year Treasury yield explicitly hit 5.10% in September.
Firms' input costs, especially fuel, spiked in September.
Federal Reserve's hawkish stance on inflation.
Weak demand at a U.S. Treasury auction.
en.why_matters: A sustained high 10-year yield impacts borrowing costs across the economy, potentially slowing growth and increasing recession risks.
en.bull_case: The 10-year Treasury yield has already reached 5.10% in September, fulfilling the market condition.
en.bear_case: If reported data proving the 5.10% hit in September is later found to be inaccurate or retracted.
